title: Where to Hear Live Music in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has live music every night, but the best moments are not the obvious ones.** The tourist listings push big ticketed shows. The things worth planning around are quieter: a free lunchtime concert, a late-night jam, a Sunday in a park.

**The single best free music moment is the Berliner Philharmonie lunch concert, Wednesdays at 1pm from September to June.** Musicians from one of the world's great orchestras play in the foyer, admission is free, and no ticket is needed. I come 30 to 40 minutes early because the numbers are capped.

**For jazz, go small.** b-flat in Mitte sits a two-minute walk from where my walking tour ends at Hackescher Markt, and A-Trane in Charlottenburg has run since 1992. A-Trane's Saturday late-night jam session is free after midnight.
**On a Sunday, Mauerpark is the live-music afternoon.** The bearpit karaoke and the buskers around the flea market are free and pure Berlin. Bring a few coins for the ones who earn it.

**In high summer, adjust.** The free Wednesday lunch concert pauses over the summer break, so I lean on the jazz clubs, Mauerpark, and the summer organ concerts at the Berliner Dom instead. Line-ups and prices change, so check the venue before you go.
